newsitem.title: USA: Navy calls off search for missing helicopter crew.
newsitem.headline: Navy calls off search for missing helicopter crew.

text.p: The Navy and Coast Guard called off their search Monday for four Marines presumed dead after their helicopter crashed in the ocean six miles (10 kms) off the southern California coast.

"The Navy and Coast Guard have exhausted all possibilities in their search for survivors," said Marine spokesman Staff Sgt. Glenn Holloway. The names of the soldiers were being withheld pending notification of next of kin.

Holloway said the Marine Corps was proceeding with its investigation of the crash, which occurred Saturday night while the helicopter, a Sea Knight CH-46 twin-rotor transport, was taking off from the USS Juneau during amphibious exercises.
The aircraft, assigned to the Marine Corps Air Base in El Toro, Calif., was carrying a pilot, co-pilot and two crewmen.
Pieces of the wreckage were pulled from the Pacific Ocean Sunday, but no bodies were found. The helicopter crashed immediately after liftoff at 9:26 p.m. PDT Saturday.

The helicopter was the second Sea Knight to crash in a month. On April 19, a Navy CH-46 crashed into the ocean off Hawaii. Its four crew members were rescued. Saturday's crash occurred one year to the day when a Sea Knight collided with an AH-1 Cobra attack helicopter over North Carolina, killing all 14 Marines on board the two aircraft.
The Sea Knight, first used in the Vietnam War, is one of the oldest military aircraft still flying and is to be replaced by the V-22 Osprey by 2001, the Pentagon has said.
